items.title: Benjie White Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: And when Professor Shank, or Shrank, would come up to hear my lessons, he'd tell me point blank, you're playing by ear, you're not reading those music.

ctx.x: Well, to get back to the very beginning, were your family musical before you?

No. Nobody in my family played a musical instrument. I started in, I studied the violin. I actually studied violin for seven years. But I never could play the thing worth a nickel. I learned music, but I never could play the violin. I used to, one of, my main trouble was I wouldn't read music. I'd play the violin all right, but everything I was playing was being played by ear. And when Professor Shank, or Shrank, would come up to hear my lessons, he'd tell me point blank, you're playing by ear, you're not reading…
How old were you when you started on violin?
